info.description:
## Overview

Time Series - Sync is designed for integration with real-time web applications, dashboards, and analytical tools where responsiveness and flexibility are critical.

## Data Point Limits

Each request is scoped to a single data point.

## Investment Limits

A maximum of **25 investment** identifiers can be passed in a single request.

## Lookback Limits

Lookback limits are determined by the type of time series observation that is returned and by the frequency of the data. 

Most data points return a series of **univariate** observations. A univariate observation consists of two fields - `date` and `value`.

Some data points, for example Daily OHLCV, return a series of **multivariate** observations. A multivariate observation consists of a date field and multiple named value fields — for example, OHLCV data includes `dailyOpenPrice`, `dailyHighPrice`, `dailyLowPrice`, `dailyClosePrice`, and `dailyVolume`.

### Lookback Limits - Univariate Observations

| Frequency | Maximum Lookback |
|-----------|-----------------|
| Daily | 12 months| 
| Weekly | 60 months | 
| Monthly | 120 months | 
| Quarterly | 600 months | 
| Annual | 600 months | 


### Lookback Limits - Multivariate Observations

| Frequency | Maximum Lookback |
|-----------|-----------------|
| All | 6 months| 


## Data Point Types

The API supports **standard** and **computed** data points.

**Standard** data points are returned directly from stored data and do not require any data-point-level parameters. Only global request parameters apply.

**Computed** data points require data-point-level parameters and output values are calculated at runtime.

## Authentication

Retrieve tokens required to authorize calls to the API. See [documentation](https://developer.morningstar.com/direct-web-services/documentation/api-utilities/authentication-api/overview).

get.summary: Get 12-Month Yield time series.
get.description: An expression of the amount paid out in distributions (pre-tax) by the investment in the last 12 months expressed as a percentage of the previous month end price.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of up to 25 investment identifiers to query.

Accepts:

- Morningstar Performance ID (default)
- Morningstar Security ID
- Morningstar IDs (MSID)
- ISIN
- CUSIP
- Trading symbol
- Category ID   
  Important: When a category ID is passed, the corresponding `identifierType` can be `performanceId` or `securityId`. The value must be URL-encoded. For example, if the category ID is `LC00002226;CA]FO`, the URL-encoded value is `LC00002226;CA%5DFO`.

parameters.name: idTypes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list specifying the type of each value passed in the `ids` parameter.
Rules: * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value * Empty values default to `performanceId` Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3` * `id1` and `id3` are performance IDs * `id2` is a security ID * `idTypes=,securityId` Accepted values: * `performanceId` (default) * `isin` * `securityId` * `cusip` * `tradingSymbol` * `msid`

parameters.name: baseCurrency
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 4217 currency codes (for example, `CAD`, `EUR`, `JPY`).
* Filters results based on currency * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5` * Base currency passed for `id2` and `id4` * `baseCurrency=,USD,,USD`

parameters.name: domicile
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`). 
Rules:

*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Domicile passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `domicile=,USA,,USA`

parameters.name: exchangeCountry
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`).


*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Exchange country passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `exchangeCountry=,USA,,USA`

parameters.name: exchangeId
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of exchange IDs (for example, `EX$$$$XMEX`, `EX$$$$XNAS`).

*   Filters results based on exchange ID
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Exchange ID passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `exchangeId=,EX$$$$XMEX,,EX$$$$XNAS`

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Specifies the time interval between data points.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Specifies the start date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Specifies the end date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: timePeriod
parameters.description:
Specifies the size of the time window for the data range. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriodUnit` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: timePeriodUnit
parameters.description:
Specifies the time period unit. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriod` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: applyEarliestCommonDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to apply the earliest common start date across all investments.

 When set to `true`, the start date of the time series is adjusted to match the latest inception date among the investments, ensuring all data points are aligned.

parameters.name: applyTrackRecordExtension
parameters.description: Specifies whether to apply the Track Record Extension logic in order to extend the performance of an investment by copying the historical performance of another qualified older investment.

parameters.name: applyRestructureDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to consider the Morningstar or Custom restructure date when determining the start of the performance period.

This option is applicable only when `applyEarliestCommonDate` is set to true.

parameters.name: sinceInception
parameters.description:
Sets the time range from inception (or the maximum supported lookback) to the end date. 

Takes precendence over any `timePeriod` / `timePeriodUnit` and `startDate` / `endDate` settings.

parameters.name: currencyId
parameters.description: Specifies the currency in which to return data.

Comma-separated list of up to 25 investment identifiers to query.

Accepts:

- Morningstar Performance ID (default)
- Morningstar Security ID
- Morningstar IDs (MSID)
- ISIN
- CUSIP
- Trading symbol
- Category ID   
  Important: When a category ID is passed, the corresponding `identifierType` can be `performanceId` or `securityId`. The value must be URL-encoded. For example, if the category ID is `LC00002226;CA]FO`, the URL-encoded value is `LC00002226;CA%5DFO`.

parameters.name: idTypes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list specifying the type of each value passed in the `ids` parameter.
Rules: * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value * Empty values default to `performanceId` Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3` * `id1` and `id3` are performance IDs * `id2` is a security ID * `idTypes=,securityId` Accepted values: * `performanceId` (default) * `isin` * `securityId` * `cusip` * `tradingSymbol` * `msid`

parameters.name: baseCurrency
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 4217 currency codes (for example, `CAD`, `EUR`, `JPY`).
* Filters results based on currency * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5` * Base currency passed for `id2` and `id4` * `baseCurrency=,USD,,USD`

parameters.name: domicile
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`). 
Rules:

*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Domicile passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `domicile=,USA,,USA`

parameters.name: exchangeCountry
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`).


*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Exchange country passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `exchangeCountry=,USA,,USA`

parameters.name: exchangeId
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of exchange IDs (for example, `EX$$$$XMEX`, `EX$$$$XNAS`).

*   Filters results based on exchange ID
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Exchange ID passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `exchangeId=,EX$$$$XMEX,,EX$$$$XNAS`

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Specifies the time interval between data points.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Specifies the start date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Specifies the end date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: timePeriod
parameters.description:
Specifies the size of the time window for the data range. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriodUnit` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: timePeriodUnit
parameters.description:
Specifies the time period unit. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriod` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: applyEarliestCommonDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to apply the earliest common start date across all investments.

 When set to `true`, the start date of the time series is adjusted to match the latest inception date among the investments, ensuring all data points are aligned.

parameters.name: applyTrackRecordExtension
parameters.description: Specifies whether to apply the Track Record Extension logic in order to extend the performance of an investment by copying the historical performance of another qualified older investment.

parameters.name: applyRestructureDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to consider the Morningstar or Custom restructure date when determining the start of the performance period.

This option is applicable only when `applyEarliestCommonDate` is set to true.

parameters.name: sinceInception
parameters.description:
Sets the time range from inception (or the maximum supported lookback) to the end date. 

Takes precendence over any `timePeriod` / `timePeriodUnit` and `startDate` / `endDate` settings.

parameters.name: currencyId
parameters.description: Specifies the currency in which to return data.

get.summary: Get Income Only Yield Price US time series.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of up to 25 investment identifiers to query.

Accepts:

- Morningstar Performance ID (default)
- Morningstar Security ID
- Morningstar IDs (MSID)
- ISIN
- CUSIP
- Trading symbol
- Category ID   
  Important: When a category ID is passed, the corresponding `identifierType` can be `performanceId` or `securityId`. The value must be URL-encoded. For example, if the category ID is `LC00002226;CA]FO`, the URL-encoded value is `LC00002226;CA%5DFO`.

parameters.name: idTypes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list specifying the type of each value passed in the `ids` parameter.
Rules: * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value * Empty values default to `performanceId` Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3` * `id1` and `id3` are performance IDs * `id2` is a security ID * `idTypes=,securityId` Accepted values: * `performanceId` (default) * `isin` * `securityId` * `cusip` * `tradingSymbol` * `msid`

parameters.name: baseCurrency
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 4217 currency codes (for example, `CAD`, `EUR`, `JPY`).
* Filters results based on currency * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5` * Base currency passed for `id2` and `id4` * `baseCurrency=,USD,,USD`

parameters.name: domicile
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`). 
Rules:

*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Domicile passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `domicile=,USA,,USA`

parameters.name: exchangeCountry
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`).


*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Exchange country passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `exchangeCountry=,USA,,USA`

parameters.name: exchangeId
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of exchange IDs (for example, `EX$$$$XMEX`, `EX$$$$XNAS`).

*   Filters results based on exchange ID
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Exchange ID passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `exchangeId=,EX$$$$XMEX,,EX$$$$XNAS`

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Specifies the time interval between data points.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Specifies the start date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Specifies the end date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: timePeriod
parameters.description:
Specifies the size of the time window for the data range. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriodUnit` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: timePeriodUnit
parameters.description:
Specifies the time period unit. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriod` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: applyEarliestCommonDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to apply the earliest common start date across all investments.

 When set to `true`, the start date of the time series is adjusted to match the latest inception date among the investments, ensuring all data points are aligned.

parameters.name: applyTrackRecordExtension
parameters.description: Specifies whether to apply the Track Record Extension logic in order to extend the performance of an investment by copying the historical performance of another qualified older investment.

parameters.name: applyRestructureDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to consider the Morningstar or Custom restructure date when determining the start of the performance period.

This option is applicable only when `applyEarliestCommonDate` is set to true.

parameters.name: sinceInception
parameters.description:
Sets the time range from inception (or the maximum supported lookback) to the end date. 

Takes precendence over any `timePeriod` / `timePeriodUnit` and `startDate` / `endDate` settings.

Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`). 
Rules:

*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Domicile passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `domicile=,USA,,USA`

Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`). 
Rules:

*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Domicile passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `domicile=,USA,,USA`

get.summary: Get Summary Risk Indicator (SRI) Value time series.
get.description: The investment's Summary Risk Indicator (SRI) denoting the level of risk calculated in accordance with the Packaged Retail and Insurance based Investment Product (PRIIP) classification.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of up to 25 investment identifiers to query.

Accepts:

- Morningstar Performance ID (default)
- Morningstar Security ID
- Morningstar IDs (MSID)
- ISIN
- CUSIP
- Trading symbol
- Category ID   
  Important: When a category ID is passed, the corresponding `identifierType` can be `performanceId` or `securityId`. The value must be URL-encoded. For example, if the category ID is `LC00002226;CA]FO`, the URL-encoded value is `LC00002226;CA%5DFO`.

parameters.name: idTypes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list specifying the type of each value passed in the `ids` parameter.
Rules: * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value * Empty values default to `performanceId` Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3` * `id1` and `id3` are performance IDs * `id2` is a security ID * `idTypes=,securityId` Accepted values: * `performanceId` (default) * `isin` * `securityId` * `cusip` * `tradingSymbol` * `msid`

parameters.name: baseCurrency
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 4217 currency codes (for example, `CAD`, `EUR`, `JPY`).
* Filters results based on currency * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5` * Base currency passed for `id2` and `id4` * `baseCurrency=,USD,,USD`

parameters.name: domicile
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`). 
Rules:

*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Domicile passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `domicile=,USA,,USA`

parameters.name: exchangeCountry
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`).


*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   Exchange country passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `exchangeCountry=,USA,,USA`

parameters.name: exchangeId
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of exchange IDs (for example, `EX$$$$XMEX`, `EX$$$$XNAS`).

*   Filters results based on exchange ID
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: Specifies the start date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Specifies the end date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: timePeriod
parameters.description:
Specifies the size of the time window for the data range. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriodUnit` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: timePeriodUnit
parameters.description:

- Used in combination with `timePeriod` to specify relative time ranges.

parameters.name: applyEarliestCommonDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to apply the earliest common start date across all investments.

 When set to `true`, the start date of the time series is adjusted to match the latest inception date among the investments, ensuring all data points are aligned.

parameters.name: applyTrackRecordExtension
parameters.description: Specifies whether to apply the Track Record Extension logic in order to extend the performance of an investment by copying the historical performance of another qualified older investment.

parameters.name: applyRestructureDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to consider the Morningstar or Custom restructure date when determining the start of the performance period.

This option is applicable only when `applyEarliestCommonDate` is set to true.

parameters.name: sinceInception
parameters.description:
Sets the time range from inception (or the maximum supported lookback) to the end date. 

Takes precendence over any `timePeriod` / `timePeriodUnit` and `startDate` / `endDate` settings.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: Specifies the end date for the time series. Accepted format is `yyyy-MM-dd`.

parameters.name: timePeriod
parameters.description:
Specifies the size of the time window for the data range. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriodUnit` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: timePeriodUnit
parameters.description:
Specifies the time period unit. 

- Used in combination with `timePeriod` to specify relative time ranges. 

- When `startDate`, `endDate`, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` are provided, `timePeriod` and `timePeriodUnit` take precedence.

parameters.name: applyEarliestCommonDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to apply the earliest common start date across all investments.

 When set to `true`, the start date of the time series is adjusted to match the latest inception date among the investments, ensuring all data points are aligned.

parameters.name: applyTrackRecordExtension
parameters.description: Specifies whether to apply the Track Record Extension logic in order to extend the performance of an investment by copying the historical performance of another qualified older investment.

parameters.name: applyRestructureDate
parameters.description:
Specifies whether to consider the Morningstar or Custom restructure date when determining the start of the performance period.

This option is applicable only when `applyEarliestCommonDate` is set to true.

parameters.name: sinceInception
parameters.description:
Sets the time range from inception (or the maximum supported lookback) to the end date. 

Takes precendence over any `timePeriod` / `timePeriodUnit` and `startDate` / `endDate` settings.

parameters.name: currencyId
parameters.description: Specifies the currency in which to return data.

get.description: The exit charge or one-time deduction paid on redemptions if the investment has been held for the recommended holding period.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of up to 25 investment identifiers to query.

Accepts:

- Morningstar Performance ID (default)
- Morningstar Security ID
- Morningstar IDs (MSID)
- ISIN
- CUSIP
- Trading symbol
- Category ID   
  Important: When a category ID is passed, the corresponding `identifierType` can be `performanceId` or `securityId`. The value must be URL-encoded. For example, if the category ID is `LC00002226;CA]FO`, the URL-encoded value is `LC00002226;CA%5DFO`.

parameters.name: idTypes
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list specifying the type of each value passed in the `ids` parameter.
Rules: * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value * Empty values default to `performanceId` Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3` * `id1` and `id3` are performance IDs * `id2` is a security ID * `idTypes=,securityId` Accepted values: * `performanceId` (default) * `isin` * `securityId` * `cusip` * `tradingSymbol` * `msid`

parameters.name: baseCurrency
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 4217 currency codes (for example, `CAD`, `EUR`, `JPY`).
* Filters results based on currency * Values must align with the order of values in `ids` * Use empty entries to skip * Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value Example: * `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5` * Base currency passed for `id2` and `id4` * `baseCurrency=,USD,,USD`

parameters.name: domicile
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of 3-character ISO 3166‑1 country codes (for example, `CAN`, `IRL`, `IND`). 
Rules:

*   Filters results based on domicile
*   Values must align with the order of values in `ids`
*   Use empty entries to skip
*   Omit trailing commas after the last non-empty value

Example:

*   `ids=id1,id2,id3,id4,id5`
*   Domicile passed for `id2` and `id4`
*   `domicile=,USA,,USA`
